lines.text: That was 2025, counting add-ons: about 25 a day. Your vet, your dentist, even your plumber could be on the list.
lines.say: That was twenty twenty-five, counting add-on deals: about twenty-five a day. Your vet, your dentist, even your plumber could be on the list.

lines.text: Worldwide, Bain counted $904 billion of buyouts in 2025, not counting add-ons.
lines.say: Worldwide, the consulting firm Bain counted nine hundred four billion dollars of buyouts in twenty twenty-five, not counting add-ons.

lines.text: That was up 44% from 2024, and second only to the record year of 2021.
lines.say: That was up forty-four percent from twenty twenty-four, and second only to the record year of twenty twenty-one.

lines.text: So who's buying, with whose money, and is it good or bad for the rest of us?
lines.say: So who's buying, with whose money, and is it good or bad for the rest of us?

lines.text: Researchers have studied it for decades, and the answer depends a lot on what got bought.
lines.say: Researchers have studied it for decades, and the answer depends a lot on what got bought.

lines.text: We'll cover how a fund works, a buyout with real math, where the money went, and what the studies found.
lines.say: We'll cover how a fund works, a buyout with real math, where the money went, and what the studies found.

lines.text: Chapter 1: How a private equity fund works.
lines.say: Chapter one: How a private equity fund works.

lines.text: Private equity means owning companies that don't trade on the stock market, sometimes by taking public ones private.
lines.say: Private equity means owning companies that don't trade on the stock market, sometimes by taking public ones private.

lines.text: It starts with a firm, called the general partner, or GP.
lines.say: It starts with a firm, called the general partner, or G P.

lines.text: The GP raises money from limited partners, or LPs: pension funds, university endowments, insurers and wealthy families.
lines.say: The G P raises money from limited partners, or L Ps: pension funds, university endowments, insurers and wealthy families.

lines.text: Big public pension funds, like CalSTRS, California's teachers' fund, put part of their money into PE funds.
lines.say: Big public pension funds, like Cal S T R S, California's teachers' fund, put part of their money into P E funds.

lines.text: The money is usually locked up for about ten years. The GP buys companies, tries to improve them, then sells them for more.
lines.say: The money is usually locked up for about ten years. The G P buys companies, tries to improve them, then sells them for more.

lines.text: For that work, the GP usually charges what's called two and twenty.
lines.say: For that work, the G P usually charges what's called two and twenty.

lines.text: The 2 is a yearly management fee, typically 1.5% to 2% of the money in the fund.
lines.say: The two is a yearly management fee, typically one and a half to two percent of the money in the fund.

lines.text: Example: on a $1 billion fund, 2% is $20 million a year, whether the deals work or not.
lines.say: For example, on a one billion dollar fund, two percent is twenty million dollars a year, whether the deals work or not.

lines.text: The 20 is carried interest: the GP's cut of the profits, usually after investors earn a minimum return, often 8% a year.
lines.say: The twenty is carried interest: the G P's cut of the profits, usually after investors earn a minimum return, often eight percent a year.

lines.text: So the GP gets paid steadily for running the fund, and paid big if the deals pay off.
lines.say: So the G P gets paid steadily for running the fund, and paid big if the deals pay off.

lines.text: Chapter 2: The leveraged buyout.
lines.say: Chapter two: The leveraged buyout.

lines.text: Here's the move that makes private equity different: buying with borrowed money.
lines.say: Here's the move that makes private equity different: buying with borrowed money.

lines.text: It's called a leveraged buyout, or LBO. Think of buying a house with a mortgage.
lines.say: It's called a leveraged buyout, or L B O. Think of buying a house with a mortgage.

lines.text: With one big twist: the loan goes on the company's books, not the fund's.
lines.say: With one big twist: the loan goes on the company's books, not the fund's.

lines.text: Let's run a hypothetical example with round numbers. A fund buys a company for $100 million.
lines.say: Let's run a hypothetical example with round numbers. A fund buys a company for one hundred million dollars.

lines.text: It puts in $40 million of its own money and borrows $60 million.
lines.say: It puts in forty million dollars of its own money and borrows sixty million dollars.

lines.text: Over five years, the company's profits pay the debt down to $40 million. Then the fund sells it for $150 million.
lines.say: Over five years, the company's profits pay the debt down to forty million dollars. Then the fund sells it for one hundred fifty million dollars.

lines.text: Subtract the $40 million still owed, and the fund keeps $110 million.
lines.say: Subtract the forty million dollars still owed, and the fund keeps one hundred ten million dollars.

lines.text: It put in $40 million, so that's 2.75 times its money, before the GP's cut.
lines.say: It put in forty million dollars, so that's two point seven five times its money, before the G P's cut.

lines.text: A buyer who paid all cash would have made 1.5 times. Same company, same sale. The debt did the rest.
lines.say: A buyer who paid all cash would have made one and a half times. Same company, same sale. The debt did the rest.

lines.text: Now the carry. The profit is $70 million, and 20% of that, $14 million, goes to the GP. The LPs get $96 million, about 2.4 times their money.
lines.say: Now the carry. The profit is seventy million dollars, and twenty percent of that, fourteen million dollars, goes to the G P. The L Ps get ninety-six million dollars, about two point four times their money.

lines.text: That's simplified. Real deals also have fees, interest and that hurdle we mentioned.
lines.say: That's simplified. Real deals also have fees, interest and that hurdle we mentioned.

lines.text: Now flip it. Say profits stall, the debt stays at $60 million, and the company sells for just $80 million.
lines.say: Now flip it. Say profits stall, the debt stays at sixty million dollars, and the company sells for just eighty million dollars.

lines.text: The fund gets $20 million back, so half its money is gone. The all-cash buyer would have lost 20%.
lines.say: The fund gets twenty million dollars back, so half its money is gone. The all-cash buyer would have lost twenty percent.

lines.text: Debt makes wins bigger and losses bigger. And if profits can't cover the payments, the company itself can go under.
lines.say: Debt makes wins bigger and losses bigger. And if profits can't cover the payments, the company itself can go under.

lines.text: Electronic Arts agreed in September 2025 to be bought for about $55 billion.
lines.say: Electronic Arts agreed in September twenty twenty-five to be bought for about fifty-five billion dollars.

lines.text: The buyers, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, lined up about $20 billion of that as debt.
lines.say: The buyers, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, lined up about twenty billion dollars of that as debt.

lines.text: Bain recorded it at $56.6 billion, the biggest buyout on record.
lines.say: Bain recorded it at fifty-six point six billion dollars, the biggest buyout on record.

lines.text: Chapter 3: Where the money went.
lines.say: Chapter three: Where the money went.

lines.text: Giant deals did a lot of the lifting. Bain counted 13 buyouts over $10 billion in 2025, worth $274 billion combined.
lines.say: Giant deals did a lot of the lifting. Bain counted thirteen buyouts over ten billion dollars in twenty twenty-five, worth two hundred seventy-four billion dollars combined.

lines.text: Meanwhile, the number of buyout deals actually fell 6%.
lines.say: Meanwhile, the number of buyout deals actually fell six percent.

lines.text: That's called a roll-up: buy one business, then keep adding similar ones nearby.
lines.say: That's called a roll-up: buy one business, then keep adding similar ones nearby.

lines.text: Take the trades. PitchBook data showed nearly 800 HVAC, plumbing and electrical firms bought by PE from 2022 to late 2024.
lines.say: Take the trades. PitchBook data showed nearly eight hundred H V A C, plumbing and electrical firms bought by P E from twenty twenty-two to late twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Dentists too. In 2024, 16.1% of US dentists were tied to a dental support organization, up from 7.2% in 2015.
lines.say: Dentists too. In twenty twenty-four, sixteen point one percent of US dentists were tied to a dental support organization, up from seven point two percent in twenty fifteen.

lines.text: Many of those groups are PE-backed. One study found PE-affiliated dentists rose from 6.6% in 2015 to 12.8% in 2021.
lines.say: Many of those groups are P E backed. One study found P E affiliated dentists rose from six point six percent in twenty fifteen to twelve point eight percent in twenty twenty-one.

lines.text: Vet clinics are another target. In 2022, the FTC required PE firm JAB Consumer Partners to sell some clinics as a condition of buying two vet chains.
lines.say: Vet clinics are another target. In twenty twenty-two, the F T C required the P E firm JAB Consumer Partners to sell some clinics as a condition of buying two vet chains.

lines.text: Those deals were worth $1.1 billion and $1.65 billion, and the FTC called it a roll-up.
lines.say: Those deals were worth one point one billion dollars and one point six five billion dollars, and the F T C called it a roll-up.

lines.text: Then there's housing. A May 2024 GAO report said 32 large investors, some PE-backed, owned about 450,000 single-family homes as of 2022.
lines.say: Then there's housing. A May twenty twenty-four G A O report said thirty-two large investors, some backed by private equity, owned about four hundred fifty thousand single-family homes as of twenty twenty-two.

lines.text: Nationally, investors with over 1,000 homes owned about 3% of single-family rentals. In Atlanta, GAO estimated about 25%.
lines.say: Nationally, investors with over a thousand homes owned about three percent of single-family rentals. In Atlanta, the G A O estimated about twenty-five percent.

lines.text: In July 2026, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law, without the president's signature.
lines.say: In July twenty twenty-six, the twenty-first Century ROAD to Housing Act became law, without the president's signature.

lines.text: Hospitals are on the list too. Take the Steward case.
lines.say: Hospitals are on the list too. Take the Steward case.

lines.say: It reported over nine billion dollars in liabilities. About six point six billion dollars were long-term lease obligations to its landlord, Medical Properties Trust.

lines.text: PE also buys software companies, like EA. And it has moved into pro sports.
lines.say: P E also buys software companies, like E A. And it has moved into pro sports.

lines.say: Bain says global healthcare P E deals hit a record one hundred ninety billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Chapter 4: The case for private equity.
lines.say: Chapter four: The case for private equity.

lines.text: Supporters say PE owners fix sleepy companies with sharper management, better systems, and owners with skin in the game.
lines.say: Supporters say P E owners fix sleepy companies with sharper management, better systems, and owners with skin in the game.

lines.text: One of the largest studies looked at thousands of US buyouts from 1980 to 2013.
lines.say: One of the largest studies looked at thousands of US buyouts from nineteen eighty to twenty thirteen.

lines.text: It found labor productivity rose 8% in two years at bought companies versus similar ones.
lines.say: It found labor productivity rose eight percent in two years at bought companies versus similar ones.

lines.text: Jobs were mixed: down 12% when a public company was taken private, up 15% when a private one was bought.
lines.say: Jobs were mixed: down twelve percent when a public company was taken private, up fifteen percent when a private one was bought.

lines.say: And average pay per worker slipped one point seven percent.

lines.text: A 2016 study of restaurant chains found that after PE buyouts, restaurants got cleaner and safer, with fewer health-code violations.
lines.say: A twenty sixteen study of restaurant chains found that after P E buyouts, restaurants got cleaner and safer, with fewer health-code violations.

lines.text: On returns, a 2014 study found US buyout funds beat the S&P 500 by 20% to 27% over a fund's life.
lines.say: On returns, a twenty fourteen study found US buyout funds beat the S and P five hundred by twenty to twenty-seven percent over a fund's life.

lines.say: That's more than three percent a year, after fees.

lines.text: Even in hospitals, a 2025 study found PE-bought hospitals got more profitable, with no sign of higher death or readmission rates for heart attack, heart failure and pneumonia patients.
lines.say: Even in hospitals, a twenty twenty-five study found P E bought hospitals got more profitable, with no sign of higher death or readmission rates for heart attack, heart failure and pneumonia patients.

lines.text: Chapter 5: The case against.
lines.say: Chapter five: The case against.

lines.text: Critics say debt and fees push owners to cut where it's hard to see, like staffing.
lines.say: Critics say debt and fees push owners to cut where it's hard to see, like staffing.

lines.say: A widely cited study is about nursing homes, published in twenty twenty-four.

lines.say: Researchers used Medicare data and found P E ownership raised patient deaths by about eleven percent.

lines.text: They tied it to fewer front-line staff hours and weaker care standards, while taxpayer spending per stay went up.
lines.say: They tied it to fewer front-line staff hours and weaker care standards, while taxpayer spending per stay went up.

lines.say: In hospitals, a twenty twenty-three JAMA study found Medicare patients at P E bought hospitals had twenty-five point four percent more hospital-acquired conditions.

lines.say: The same report said buyout fundraising fell sixteen percent in twenty twenty-five, to three hundred ninety-five billion dollars.

lines.text: Chapter 6: The recap.
lines.say: Chapter six: The recap.

lines.text: Private equity firms raise money from pensions and other big investors, then buy companies, often with lots of debt.
lines.say: Private equity firms raise money from pensions and other big investors, then buy companies, often with lots of debt.

lines.say: They charge yearly fees plus a share of the profits, the classic two and twenty.

post.title: Private equity did 9,000+ US deals in 2025. How it works, and what studies found
post.ig: Over 9,000 US private equity deals in one year. Here's how it works.
post.tiktok: 9,000 private equity deals in one year. Who's buying, and with whose money?
post.yt_desc:
Private equity did more than 9,000 US deals in 2025 (PitchBook, including add-ons), about 25 a day, from vet clinics and dental offices to plumbers, homes, hospitals, software and sports teams. This video explains from zero how a PE fund works (GPs, LPs and 2 and 20), walks through a hypothetical leveraged buyout with the full math, and compares global buyout value in 2024 and 2025 (Bain, excluding add-ons). Then it lays out what peer-reviewed research found on both sides: productivity gains and cleaner restaurants, but higher death rates in PE-owned nursing homes and more hospital-acquired conditions after hospital buyouts.
